$comment: The one motion duration scale of cmux NEXT (Leo 2026-10-20: "animations all around are a bit slow"). Every timed fade and every structural move ends within one of these steps; anything entering eases out, and a selection that travels may ride the one spring (a CSS linear() easing; the native side keeps its own spring physics, so the Swift copy has no spring). scripts/cmux-next/gen-motion-scale.py writes the Swift (MotionScale.generated.swift), CSS (--cmux-motion-<step> in webviews/src/pages/shared/desktop.css) and TypeScript (webviews/src/motion/scale.generated.ts) copies. Loops (spinners, breathing) and hover-intent delays are not transitions and stay off the scale.

steps.name: quick
steps.for: hover and pressed fills, focus rings, anything leaving (a popup, a notice, a row)

steps.name: micro
steps.for: small things arriving: a fade in, a popup opening, a chip, a tooltip

steps.name: standard
steps.for: structural changes: a row or card moving, a fold opening, a scrim

steps.name: large
steps.for: the largest moves, and the ceiling: a split, a zoom, a window closing, the launch mark

spring.for: a selection or view that travels to where it lands and settles with a touch of give (a sliding tab indicator, the chat switch); run over its step (large, 240 ms) it is visibly settled by 58% (about 140 ms) and at rest by the end
